tree.title: Home

vars.heroMessage: A clean, fast, dark-first docs theme for PRSS. Grouped sidebar navigation, an on-page table of contents, copyable code blocks, and callouts — everything you need to write great docs.

tree.content:
Fast to write

Every page is a normal PRSS page. Type, drop in a code block or a callout, and publish.

Organized

Group pages into sections. The sidebar and previous/next links are generated for you.

Reader-friendly

An automatic “On this page” outline, dark mode, and a keyboard-accessible layout.

children.title: Getting Started
children.content: Everything you need to stand up a documentation site with PRSS. Start with the introduction, then install and ship your first page.

children.title: Introduction
children.content:
This starter is a fully working documentation site. Edit these pages, add your own, and organize them into sections — the navigation, table of contents, and previous/next links all update automatically.

What you get

  • Grouped sidebar generated from your site structure.
  • On-page outline built from the headings you write.
  • Code blocks with one-click copy.
  • Callouts for notes, tips, and warnings.
Tip: Every item in the sidebar is just a page. Add a page under a section and it appears here instantly.

How pages are organized

Sections are pages that contain other pages. The theme renders the top level of your structure as sidebar groups and their children as links.

Next steps

Head to Installation to learn how to add and arrange pages.

children.title: Installation
children.content:
You don't install anything to use this theme — it ships with PRSS. This page shows how to add content.

Add a page

Create a new page and place it under a section to make it appear in the sidebar.

Write with blocks or HTML

Use the editor's headings, lists, code, and callout blocks. Headings become entries in the “On this page” outline.

Heads up: Keep one h1 per page (the title is added for you) and use h2/h3 for sections.

children.title: Quick Start
children.content:
Publish your first documented feature in three steps.

1. Create a section

Add a page named after your topic (for example, “Guides”). It becomes a sidebar group.

2. Add pages under it

Create child pages for each article. They appear as links under the group.

3. Preview and deploy

Use PRSS preview to review, then deploy to your host of choice.

Done! Your docs site is live with working navigation and search-friendly pages.

The theme is dark-first with a light mode toggle. Colors are driven by CSS variables so you can rebrand quickly.

Brand color

children.title: Deployment
children.content:
Ship your docs anywhere PRSS can deploy.

Preview locally

Use PRSS preview to review the built site before publishing.

Publish

Connect a host in Site Settings and deploy. Every build regenerates the sidebar and outline from your current pages.

Tip: Keep section names short — they become the sidebar group headers.

children.title: Introducing the PRSS Docs theme

vars.excerpt: A dark-first, structure-driven documentation theme — sidebar, table of contents, and previous/next all build themselves.

children.content:
Today we're shipping a documentation theme for PRSS that does the tedious parts for you. There are no menus to hand-build: the sidebar is derived from your site structure, and the on-page outline is built from your headings.

Why structure-driven

Most docs themes make you maintain a separate navigation file. This one reads your pages directly, so adding a page under a section is all it takes to see it in the nav.

What's included

Grouped sidebar, on-page TOC, copyable code blocks, callouts, a blog, and an automatic project showcase.

children.title: How auto-navigation works

vars.excerpt: The sidebar, breadcrumbs, and previous/next links are generated from your content tree — no configuration required.

children.content:
When you build the site, the theme walks your structure to produce the sidebar. Deep product trees get their own scoped sidebar; a small docs set shows every section as a group.

Previous and next

The theme flattens the sidebar into reading order and links each page to its neighbours automatically.

children.title: Writing great docs with blocks

vars.excerpt: Callouts, code blocks, and tables you can drop into any page from the PRSS editor.

children.content:
Documentation lives and dies by its examples. Use code blocks for snippets, callouts for tips and warnings, and tables for options.

Tip: Headings become entries in the “On this page” outline automatically.
